strings.name: Gerhard Richter
strings.summary: Trained in Dresden and Düsseldorf, Richter questions how painting, photography and historical images construct perceptions of reality. Blurred photo-based paintings address familial and political memory, while color charts, squeegees and glass support abstract experiments. October 18, 1977, Birkenau and Cologne Cathedral’s window demonstrate different paths through these concerns. After stopping oil painting, he continued work on paper and in other media.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1932–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored images, memory and history between photo-based painting and abstraction, exerting a lasting influence on postwar painting and contemporary art practice.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Images and historical memory
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: October 18, 1977 and Birkenau use transformations between photography and painting to question how historical events can be represented.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Figuration alongside abstraction
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From blurred photo-based paintings to color charts, squeegee paintings and glass, he investigates images, surfaces and perception.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Landschaften opens in New York
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Curated in close collaboration with the artist, the exhibition placed photo-based landscapes alongside abstractions and included loans from his collection.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: A major Paris retrospective opens
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Fondation Louis Vuitton surveyed more than six decades of his practice in an exhibition continuing into March 2026.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Creates Birkenau
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Photographs from a concentration camp became overpainted abstractions addressing Holocaust memory and the limits of representation.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Cologne Cathedral window is unveiled
strings.timeline.event-04.text: A grid of colored squares fills the south transept window, linking color and chance with light in a religious interior.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Creates October 18, 1977
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Fifteen gray paintings based on photographs connected with the Red Army Faction examine political violence and memory through blurred images.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Presents 48 Portraits in Venice
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Portraits based on photographs of male intellectual and cultural figures addressed portraiture and cultural memory in the German Pavilion.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Participates in Capitalist Realism
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Collaborations with Polke, Lueg and others examined consumer images and realism within postwar West German art.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Moves from East Germany to Düsseldorf
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Moving to West Germany and returning to art school allowed him to rebuild his practice amid different artistic institutions and image cultures.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Enters the Dresden Academy
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Mural-painting studies provided early training; his later move across Germany prompted a renewed examination of images and painting.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Dresden
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Dresden, he experienced war and postwar division; family photographs and German history later became important artistic materials.
